input.quote: (ii) Either Party may, without consent of the other Party, assign this Agreement in whole to (i) in the case of RevMed, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in the case of a Change of Control or (ii) in the case of Sanofi, its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser, as applicable, in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction.
input.rationale:
Section 15.2 substantially meets our preferred position. Sanofi may assign to any Affiliate without RevMed's consent (15.2(a)(i)) and may assign in whole, without consent, to a successor or purchaser in a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction (15.2(a)(ii)) - the full affiliate/M&A carve-out. RevMed, by contrast, needs Sanofi's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments, and may not assign or transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without Sanofi's consent (15.2(b)). Critically, no RevMed right is triggered by a Sanofi Change of Control: RevMed's termination rights (12.2(b)-(e): material breach, insolvency, Sanofi Competing Product, cessation of activity) contain no change-of-control trigger, and there is no vendor exit or re-pricing on our change of control during the term. Two points noted but not flagged: (1) RevMed may assign in whole on its own Change of Control without our consent, short of the preferred "consent / never to a competitor" formulation, but mitigated by RevMed's advance notice obligation and our option to terminate (or elect the 12.2(a)(ii)B alternative) on a RevMed Change of Control, plus the firewall conditions in 15.2 (separateness of Competing Product activities, no Know-How exchange, Acquiror Family IP excluded) - this sits at or above the mutual-successor-assignment fallback; (2) the post-termination royalty payable to us under 12.3(c) ends on a Change of Control of Sanofi, and 9.7(a) allocates to us the withholding gross-up arising from a Sanofi affiliate assignment - minor sub-elements of separate financial terms rather than assignment restrictions. No redline required.</rationale>
